blocks.text: Condo buildings in Deer Lake
Streets, schools and getting around Deer Lake

items.t: The City publishes no street-by-street written boundary for the MLS sub-area; the area is generally the streets around the lake — Canada Way / Deer Lake Parkway to the north, Sperling Avenue to the east, and the Buckingham Heights slope at the lake's east and south sides — with exact MLS boundary streets UNVERIFIED. Main roads: Canada Way and Deer Lake Parkway on the north side, Sperling Avenue down the park's east side, and Buckingham Drive / Buckingham Avenue on the slope.

Where the condo stock concentrates: nowhere inside this sub-area —. The housing is detached houses around the lake and on the Buckingham Heights slope, plus heritage-register houses along Sperling Avenue inside the Deer Lake Park Heritage Precinct (for example the Woodward House at 5195 Sperling Avenue, built 1912).

Transit: there is no SkyTrain station inside the Deer Lake sub-area; the park is reached by turning off Canada Way onto Sperling Ave. Do not import neighbouring areas' stations into a Deer Lake listing — in particular, Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station serves the Sperling-Duthie / Burnaby Lake side north of the lake, not a Deer Lake address, and any transit claim for a specific property should be checked against TransLink sources for that address.
Burnaby community-level condos & townhomes that month: median sale price $686,000, $763/sqft, 98% sale-to-list, 36 days on market — a city-wide Burnaby figure, not a Deer Lake figure.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Deer Lake

items.t: Burnaby zoning — the rule that could create strata here: Burnaby consolidated its former single- and two-family districts into one R1 Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (SSMUH) District in June 2024 — R1 lots may hold 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 units on larger lots, and 6 units on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop, and lots with two or more primary units may be stratified. The governing bylaw is the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026, adopted June 9, 2026 and in effect July 1, 2026 — the former Zoning Bylaw No. 4742 (1965) is not the current bylaw and must not be cited as current.

Burnaby plan framework: the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan, adopted December 9, 2025, replaces the 1998 OCP and takes precedence over older community-plan land use maps where they conflict; Burnaby's community plans are policy guidelines for rezoning and development applications.

Heritage overlay: Sperling Avenue fronting the park lies within the Deer Lake Park Heritage Precinct and listed properties carry heritage review — a constraint on the multiplex/stratification math for precinct lots specifically.

blocks.text: Good to know about Deer Lake

items.t: The boardwalk by the boat launch is closed for a full replacement. The City closed that section of boardwalk from September 21, 2026, with completion scheduled by winter 2027 and a signed detour via Sperling Avenue and Deer Lake Drive (about five extra minutes of walking); a small section of the nearby picnic area is also closed during construction — a park-edge seller should disclose it before a buyer finds the fencing.

Burnaby's rulebook changed under this area twice in two years. The R1 SSMUH district arrived in June 2024, the Burnaby 2050 OCP was adopted December 9, 2025 (replacing the 1998 OCP and overriding older community-plan maps where they conflict), and the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 took effect July 1, 2026 — any Deer Lake document still citing the 1965 Zoning Bylaw No. 4742 or the 1998 OCP is two generations out of date.

City Hall is the sub-area's north-west neighbour. Burnaby City Hall is at 4949 Canada Way, just north-west of the sub-area — the civic precinct, Burnaby Hospital at 3935 Kincaid St to the west, and the Bob Prittie Metrotown library branch serving this quadrant are the working amenities; there is no enclosed mall or shopping centre inside the sub-area.
The heritage houses are working artist residences.
Zero attached stock is a standing condition, not a slow month.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Deer Lake
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Established park-side house lots: Buckingham Heights, the prestige pocket on the slope east of the lake, holds the large custom and estate-style homes; the flatter streets north and west of the lake hold the balance.

Lot character: typical lot sizes are UNVERIFIED at sub-area level — no official source read states them, and the research records only that Buckingham Heights slope lots are "understood locally" to be among Burnaby's larger residential lots, which is not an official-source statement and is not published here as a size. The only lot-size figures a source states are the R1 SSMUH thresholds: 280 m² and 281 m². Heritage stock is part of the lot character on Sperling Avenue: heritage-register properties cluster inside the Deer Lake Park Heritage Precinct, including the Woodward House at 5195 Sperling Avenue, built 1912.

Serviced position, as the City states it: Burnaby's 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where applicable and a residential garbage toter fee; the detached single-family dwelling water charge is $652.33, rates carry a 5% discount if paid by the due date, and for single-family homes sewer is billed as a sewer parcel tax on the property tax notice. Confirm servicing for the specific parcel with the City.

ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in Deer Lake is confirmed in the research; ALR status is a property-specific check through the Agricultural Land Commission, UNVERIFIED for individual lots. No ALR percentage split is stated.

What a "Deer Lake land/attached" search actually returns — documented, NOT counted: detached houses in Buckingham Heights, heritage houses on Sperling Avenue, and attached product in neighbouring sub-areas (Burnaby Lake, Sperling-Duthie, Metrotown, Forest Glen, Upper Deer Lake, Deer Lake Place) whose listings use "Deer Lake" as a lifestyle reference while their own MLS area fields name the neighbouring sub-area. None is Deer Lake stock.

Market context, labelled correctly: Burnaby IS a SnapStats-covered community — Detached versus "Condos & Townhomes" combined only. SnapStats has NO land category, and no detached figure is a land figure. September 2026 context only: Deer Lake sub-area detached inventory 13 / solds 1 (8% ratio) and "Condos & Townhomes" 0 / 0; Burnaby community detached median $1,825,000 and attached median $686,000. Sub-area medians are UNVERIFIED (community level only).

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Deer Lake

items.t: Deer Lake is a City of Burnaby sub-area in central Burnaby — the residential streets around Deer Lake Park, east of Burnaby City Hall and south of Canada Way, with the park's main address at 6450 Deer Lake Ave. "Deer Lake" is the GVR board sub-area name used in the SnapStats GVR report for Burnaby, distinct in that report from "Deer Lake Place" and "Upper Deer Lake," which are separate sub-areas. The City publishes no street-by-street written boundary for the MLS sub-area; the area is generally the streets around the lake between Canada Way / Deer Lake Parkway to the north, Sperling Avenue to the east, and the Buckingham Heights slope at the lake's east and south sides — exact MLS boundary streets are UNVERIFIED.
Nearby areas: Sperling-Duthie to the north and east, Burnaby Hospital to the west, Buckingham Heights within and beside the east side, Forest Glen and Metrotown to the south-west.

Main roads: Canada Way and Deer Lake Parkway run along the north side; Sperling Avenue runs down the park's east side; Buckingham Drive / Buckingham Avenue serve the slope streets east of the lake. There is no SkyTrain station inside the sub-area; the park is reached by turning off Canada Way onto Sperling Ave. Burnaby City Hall is at 4949 Canada Way, just north-west. Commute times in minutes: UNVERIFIED.

The park is the sub-area: the City describes Deer Lake Park as a peaceful natural environment serving as the cultural centre of the city, its trails connecting the lake, Burnaby Art Gallery, Shadbolt Centre for the Arts, Burnaby Village Museum (6501 Deer Lake Ave) and Hart House restaurant; the park is open dawn to dusk year-round. The nearest library branch is the Bob Prittie Metrotown Branch; the city's hospital, Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St, is immediately west.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Deer Lake

items.t: Heritage and lakeshore diligence: Sperling Avenue fronting the park lies within the Deer Lake Park Heritage Precinct, and heritage-register houses such as the 1912 Woodward House carry heritage review — check the register and the precinct before planning a rebuild or subdivision on a park-fronting lot. A floodplain designation for Deer Lake's residential streets was not confirmed in the sources read; the lakeshore is the area's wet edge (the City is replacing the boat-launch boardwalk outright), and parcel-level hazard status is a property-specific check: UNVERIFIED lot by lot.

items.t: The boardwalk by the boat launch is closed from September 21, 2026 for a full replacement, with completion scheduled by winter 2027 and a signed detour via Sperling Avenue and Deer Lake Drive (about five extra minutes of walking); a small section of the nearby picnic area is also closed during construction — park-fronting lots carry that window in their trail access.

There is no City recreation facility verified inside the sub-area itself: the nearest City recreation centres are at Metrotown and the Burnaby Lake side — a Deer Lake lot's recreation offer is the park, not a centre.

faq.q: What is in Deer Lake Park?
faq.a: Walking trails and a boardwalk around the lake, a boat launch and picnic areas, and Burnaby's cultural precinct: the Shadbolt Centre for the Arts, the Burnaby Art Gallery, Burnaby Village Museum and Hart House restaurant, all connected by the park's trails; the park is open dawn to dusk year-round.

faq.q: Is Deer Lake the same sub-area as Deer Lake Place or Upper Deer Lake?
faq.a: No. In the SnapStats GVR report, Deer Lake, Deer Lake Place and Upper Deer Lake are three separate Burnaby sub-areas with separate inventory and solds; Deer Lake itself recorded 13 detached listings, 1 detached sold and no attached listings in September 2026 (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: What should I check before renovating a house near the lake?
faq.a: Whether the property is on the City's heritage register or inside the Deer Lake Park Heritage Precinct on Sperling Avenue — listed houses such as the 1912 Woodward House at 5195 Sperling Avenue carry heritage review — and the parcel's zone and R1 SSMUH eligibility under the 2026 Zoning Bylaw.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Deer Lake?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 13 houses listed with 1 sold in the month in Deer Lake. Those are month-end counts and move daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Deer Lake a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In September 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 8%, a buyers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: Are there any condos in Deer Lake at all?
faq.a: A buyer set on strata living near the lake is shopping the neighbouring sub-areas, not this one.

faq.q: Is Deer Lake Place or Upper Deer Lake the same thing?
faq.a: No. In the SnapStats GVR report, Deer Lake, Deer Lake Place and Upper Deer Lake are three separate Burnaby sub-areas with separate inventory and solds — attached product filed under the other two names is not Deer Lake product.

faq.q: A listing near the lake calls itself a Deer Lake townhouse. Should I believe the label?
faq.a: The Deer Lake sub-area's own attached count is zero.

faq.q: Could a Deer Lake house lot become strata homes?
faq.a: Potentially, under the citywide R1 SSMUH district: 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 on larger lots, 6 on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop, and lots with two or more primary units may be stratified — but heritage-precinct and park-edge lots carry extra review, so eligibility is lot by lot under the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026.

faq.q: If a small Deer Lake multiplex is stratified, does it need a depreciation report?
faq.a: Only if it has five or more lots: since July 1, 2024 stratas with 5+ lots must obtain one every five years, and stratas with four or fewer lots are exempt. A 3- or 4-unit strata here could be exempt — which makes the Form B and the strata's own financials the whole diligence picture.
